The path-to-throne and elevation sequence contacts the focus's great transgression and great magnitude; the reading remains a spatialized inference, not a literal ascent claim.

The seeking, proximity, hope, fear, caution, harm-removal, and state-change traces support a direction-dependent response. The focus's moral transgression does not meet the water, sea, blood, sound, or wind subjects of the overflow branch.

findings.title: Encompassed audience, diagnostic vision
findings.claim: The audience stands within the Lord's encompassing knowledge as the shown vision and Qur'anic tree function as tests; the warning makes the response visible, but that response may turn toward caution or toward greater transgression.
findings.mechanism: The focus says the people are encompassed, then pairs a shown vision with fitna, a tree in the Qur'an, and fear-induction. The surrounding knowledge in 17:54-55 supplies the encompassing frame; 17:59 supplies a visible sign mishandled after denial, 17:57 supplies fear joined to hope and caution, and 17:41 supplies the counter-effect pattern of communication met by increased aversion. The literal tree and the interlaced-conflict branch can coexist as a contextual resonance.
findings.reader_payoff: The test is not only an event presented to an audience: it is a diagnostic whose reception becomes legible within an encompassing field, with warning capable of restraint or overflow.
findings.containment: The tree remains a tree in the primary reading; the dispute branch is an added contextual model. The text does not say the dream branch is active, that the vision is sleep-produced, or that warning mechanically causes transgression. The response may also be read without the macro-channel synthesis.

epistemic.reason: The contact is evidenced in the packet, but its macro-level synthesis remains interpretive and is kept attributed or qualified.

findings.title: Repeated countereffect in reception
findings.claim: The focus sharpens a pericope pattern: communication intended to prompt recollection or warning is received in a way that increases aversion and then crosses into great transgression.
findings.mechanism: In 17:41, Qur'anic material is varied for recollection, yet the only increase is aversion; the focus replaces that varied reminder with vision, tree, and warning, while retaining the increase operator and intensifying the output to great transgression. Before: the focus's warning appears to cause a one-time worsening. After: the matched communication-and-increase structure makes it a possible recurrence of a receiver-side transformation. The shared wording supports this reading; two independent descriptions remain possible.
findings.reader_payoff: The paradox becomes a repeated reception pattern rather than an isolated failure, while the earlier aversion remains distinct from the focus's active overflow.
findings.containment: The traced reminder, recitation, variation, increase, and withdrawal roles are all attributed to the legacy HFT record. This does not establish that the two passages describe the same recipients or that one caused the other.

epistemic.reason: The contact is evidenced in the packet, but its macro-level synthesis remains interpretive and is kept attributed or qualified.

findings.title: Counterfeit vertical greatness
findings.claim: The hypothetical route toward the elevated throne and God's great elevation give the focus's great transgression a possible spatial contour: an attempted rise that exceeds its proper limit within a field already encompassed.
findings.mechanism: The HFT trace links seeking, throne, path, elevation, and the repeated adjective kabiran to focus tughyanan kabiran. Before: great transgression is severe disobedience without a spatial mechanism. After: the parallel greatness and preceding vertical sequence allow it to read as counterfeit upward overreach. The trusted channel branch and 17:54-55 knowledge statements add an encompassing frame around that attempted reach.
findings.reader_payoff: The magnitude of the focus's transgression becomes perceptible as a false claim to height while the basic moral meaning of overstepping remains intact.
findings.containment: The verticalization is an inference from a shared adjective and the throne-path sequence; كبيرًا may simply intensify two unrelated nouns. No literal ascent, rival deity, or successful challenge is asserted. The extra encompassing branch names complete reach and knowledge, not possession of people as property.

findings.title: Disclosure through an occluded interface
findings.claim: The focus's shown vision and test can be read against a layered reception apparatus: recitation meets a concealed barrier, covered hearts, weighted ears, and turning away, so disclosure and occlusion coexist.

Before: the focus's signs are clear inputs that people consciously reject. After: the signs test a layered interface through which disclosure and concealment coexist. The focus's showing and fitna forms contact that earlier apparatus. The barrier may still describe only the earlier recitation scene.
findings.reader_payoff: The audience's increased transgression becomes an output of a reception surface, not simply a verdict that visible evidence was absent or consciously refused.
findings.containment: Every HFT role and coordinate remains attributed. The packet supports the prior barrier directly; applying that same interface to the vision and tree is an inference, and the alternative that the barrier belongs only to recitation remains live.

epistemic.reason: The contact is evidenced in the packet, but its macro-level synthesis remains interpretive and is kept attributed or qualified.

findings.title: A counter-image factory
findings.claim: The pericope depicts active reframing: people hear, counsel privately, label the messenger, strike similitudes, and stray; the focus's shown vision and tree can therefore meet rival representations rather than mere inattention.
findings.mechanism: The sequence moves from listening in 17:47 to private counsel and a counter-description, then to inspecting, striking similitudes, and straying in 17:48. Before: people remain unmoved by the vision and tree. After: recipients can metabolize signs into rival representations, one possible route by which warning is met with greater transgression. An additional focus fitna branch makes misdirection a possible result of the test without making the sign itself deceptive.
findings.reader_payoff: The focus's image-bearing forms become active sites of interpretive competition, and the recipient's reframing becomes visible as part of the response.
findings.containment: The HFT trace is legacy-unbound. The labels may answer the messenger generally rather than the focus's exact vision or tree; the sign itself is not called misleading, and the tree's literal reading remains available.

findings.title: An assay of imagined resistance

The full alternative remains that the material sequence serves only the resurrection argument.
findings.reader_payoff: The test is tied to a concrete prior image of resistance and to a response that even imagined material hardness cannot prevent.
findings.containment: All nonfocus branch roles are attributed. Iron supplies a hardness image, not a claim of smelting: the focus has no fire or gold/silver separation cue. The resurrection argument remains intact and may be the sole purpose of the material list.

findings.title: Social branching through speech

findings.title: Fear does not determine direction
findings.claim: Fear is not a deterministic stimulus: 17:57 pairs it with hope, proximity-seeking, and caution, while the focus's warning is followed by increased transgression; reception direction changes the outcome.
findings.mechanism: The invoked beings cannot uncover harm or transform it, and are themselves described as seeking proximity, hoping for mercy, fearing punishment, and exercising caution. Before: warning itself appears to drive people into transgression. After: the same fear vocabulary participates in opposed response sequences, making orientation a possible mediator. An alternative is that worship and warning are unrelated contexts rather than a designed contrast.
findings.reader_payoff: The warning's effect is no longer treated as mechanically caused by fear; the relation of the recipient to what is feared remains perceptible.
findings.containment: The HFT comparison is legacy-unbound and its cross-context relation is qualified. The focus's tughyanan uses the moral boundary-crossing branch; the incompatible physical-overflow branch is excluded. No universal psychology is claimed.

epistemic.reason: The contact is evidenced in the packet, but its macro-level synthesis remains interpretive and is kept attributed or qualified.

findings.title: A restrained sign regime
findings.claim: The focus's vision and Qur'anic tree belong to a pericope sequence in which signs are restricted after earlier denial, a visible she-camel is wrongfully handled, and signs are sent as warning rather than as an endless spectacle contest.
findings.mechanism: A written horizon of destruction and punishment in 17:58 leads to a restriction on sending signs because earlier peoples denied them in 17:59; a manifest she-camel is seen and wrongfully treated, and the verse closes by naming fear-warning as the purpose of signs. Before: the vision and tree are arbitrary tests whose warning happens to fail. After: they can be read as mediated signs within a restrained historical regime, continuing a pattern of adverse reception. The immediate alternative is that 17:59 and 17:60 are separate examples.
findings.reader_payoff: The focus's adverse response becomes part of a larger account of how warning signs are bounded and received, not a demand for ever greater spectacle.
findings.containment: The historical and regime-level connection comes through a legacy-unbound trace. The focus vision is not itself asserted to be the public she-camel sign or a punishment; the tree remains named in the Qur'an, and ordinary readings remain available.

epistemic.reason: The contact is evidenced in the packet, but its macro-level synthesis remains interpretive and is kept attributed or qualified.

findings.title: A written judgment horizon
findings.claim: The pericope's horizon of written communal destruction gives the focus's encompassing, fitna, and great transgression a bounded accountability resonance: the test and its response occur against grave judgment, not an unlimited sign contest.
findings.mechanism: The focus supplies encompassing people, test, and great transgression as carriers. The trigger is the preceding statement that towns are written for destruction or punishment before the Resurrection, followed by the restricted sign policy in 17:59. The focus's encompassing branch, fitna as trial that may include punishment, and kabir as serious wrongdoing then contact that horizon.
findings.reader_payoff: The warning acquires a local scale of accountability without turning the focus into a prediction that its audience will imminently be destroyed.
findings.containment: This uses focus branch options with an attributed legacy contextual trace. It is not a legal classification of a major sin, a prediction of imminent destruction, or a claim that the vision itself is punishment; 17:58-59 may also function as a separate historical frame.

epistemic.reason: The contact is evidenced in the packet, but its macro-level synthesis remains interpretive and is kept attributed or qualified.
